uncited: **Evaluate Base Turbulence**: Calculate the turbulence value at the texture point: $\text{turb} = \text{fast\_turbulence}(\text{pnt})$.
Map this to a base density using the power table.
**Calculate Spherical Distance Factor**: Compute the vector from the volume center to the world point: $\text{diff} = \text{pnt\_world} - \text{vol.shape.center}$.

**Add Spatial Noise Offset**: Calculate an index into the offset table based on the sum of the texture point coordinates: $\text{indx} = \lfloor (\text{pnt}.x + \text{pnt}.y + \text{pnt}.z) \times 100 \rfloor \ \& \ (\text{OFFSET\_SIZE} - 1)$.

**Apply Cosine Ramp Falloff**: If `density_max` exceeds the threshold $0.25$ (25% from center), compute the ramp index: $i = \lfloor (\text{density\_max} - 0.25) \times \frac{4}{3} \times \text{RAMP\_SIZE} \rfloor$.
If `ZoneIndex` is `(0, 0, -1)`, calculate radial falloff: $r = \sqrt{P.X^2 + P.Y^2 + P.Z^2}$.
Time and memory complexity are not given in the sources.
When not to use: When the volume shape is not roughly spherical or slab-like, or when complex internal structure requires more than a simple radial falloff.
It was designed to correct the unnatural appearance of basic turbulence-based gases by confining them to a slab and adding a rising/falloff characteristic.
